title: Sections of an fpqc form of a locally finitely presented scheme commute with qcqs affine-transition limits
statement:
Let $S$ and $A$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $p:A\to S$ be flat, surjective and quasi-compact, so $\{p\}$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Let $F:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be a contravariant functor satisfying the covering equalizer condition for every fpqc covering. Suppose its restriction to $A$-schemes is represented by an $A$-scheme $P$ locally of finite presentation [def-pc-representable-functor, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated $S$-schemes with affine transition morphisms [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ with its specified projections [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Then restriction induces a bijection of sets
$$\varinjlim_i F(Z_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(Z).$$
Here the colimit is the filtered colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Equivalently every section over $Z$ comes from a stage, and any two stage sections with the same restriction to $Z$ agree at a sufficiently late common stage. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or separatedness hypothesis on $P$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, implication (1) to (3), combined with the fpqc covering equalizer condition; agent extraction of the continuity assertion in Raynaud, Theorem 4.1, reduction 3, printed p.5-19.

proof.text: Put $U_i=Z_i\times_S A$ and $V_i=U_i\times_{Z_i}U_i$, with projections $d_{1,i},d_{2,i}:V_i\to U_i$. The affine-scheme lemma makes $S$ and $A$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By the morphism-permanence lemma (1), $p:A\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; by (3), so is $U_i\to Z_i$, and by (2) its source $U_i$ is qcqs. Likewise $V_i\to U_i$ is the base change of $U_i\to Z_i$, so another application of (3) and (2) makes $V_i$ qcqs. This uses the absolute qcqs hypotheses on $Z_i$, not a separation property of $P$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, hypothesis checks for applying (1) implies (3) after the covering base change; Schemes Tags 03GI, 01KV, 01KU, 01K5.

proof.text: Set $U=Z\times_S A$ and $V=U\times_ZU$. The transition $U_j\to U_i$ is the base change of $Z_j\to Z_i$, hence affine. Identifying $V_i$ with $Z_i\times_S(A\times_S A)$ by the fibre-product universal property shows that $V_j\to V_i$ is also a base change of $Z_j\to Z_i$, hence affine. Both systems have the required limits $U$ and $V$: a compatible family of maps $H\to U_i$ is precisely a compatible family $H\to Z_i$ and a single map $H\to A$ with equal composites to $S$. The latter map is independent of $i$ since any two indices have a common upper bound. The limit property of $Z$ identifies this with a map $H\to Z$ together with that map to $A$, hence a unique map to $U$. Replacing $A$ by $A\times_S A$ gives the same verification for $V$. These identifications preserve all projections. Give every $U_i,U$ its projection to $A$ and every $V_i,V$ the $A$-structure through $d_1$; all transition and limit maps are $A$-morphisms.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, preparation of the two base-changed systems; Morphisms Tag 01SD and the fibre-product and limit universal properties.

proof.text: The covering-base-change lemma makes $U_i\to Z_i$ and $U\to Z$ fpqc coverings, because $p$ is an fpqc covering by hypothesis. The assumed covering equalizer condition therefore identifies $F(Z_i)$ with $\operatorname{Eq}(F(U_i)\rightrightarrows F(V_i))$ and $F(Z)$ with $\operatorname{Eq}(F(U)\rightrightarrows F(V))$, the two arrows being pullback along $d_1,d_2$. In particular restriction to $U_i$ or $U$ is injective and every matching section descends uniquely. These equalizers commute with every transition and limit restriction: each square of schemes with $d_r$, for $r=1,2$, commutes by its two projections, and applying the contravariant functor $F$ gives the corresponding equality of functions.

source.place: Tag 01ZC combined with the assumed fpqc covering equalizer condition; Topologies Tag 022D, lemma-fpqc (3).

proof.text: Fix the given natural bijections $\theta_H:F(H)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_A(H,P)$ on $A$-schemes. For any $A$-morphism $e:H'\to H$, naturality says $\theta_{H'}(F(e)(x))=\theta_H(x)\circ e$. This applies to both systems of Step 2. Also $P\to A$ is locally of finite type: a finite polynomial presentation on the affine neighbourhoods in the locally-finite-presentation definition supplies finitely many algebra generators. This is the local finite type condition on those neighbourhoods. Thus the eventual-equality lemma for locally finite type morphisms applies with target $P$ and base $A$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, (1) implies (3), interpretation as Hom sets; Morphisms Tags 01TP and 01T1 for the immediate finite-presentation to finite-type implication.

proof.text: For $s\in F(Z)$ let $x\in F(U)$ be its restriction. Apply the finite-presentation map-factorization lemma to $\theta_U(x):U\to P$ over $A$, using Steps 1 and 2. It gives $i$ and $a_i:U_i\to P$ over $A$ with pullback $\theta_U(x)$. Put $x_i=\theta_{U_i}^{-1}(a_i)$. Let $b_i=F(d_{1,i})(x_i)$ and $c_i=F(d_{2,i})(x_i)$ in $F(V_i)$. Their restrictions to $V$ agree: by Step 3 they are the two restrictions of the matching section $x$. Via $\theta_{V_i}$ and $\theta_V$ this is equality of the restrictions of two $A$-maps $V_i\to P$. Apply the eventual-equality lemma to the $V_i$ system to obtain $j\ge i$ where these maps agree. By naturality and Step 3, $x_j=x_i|_{U_j}$ now has equal restrictions along $d_{1,j},d_{2,j}$; it descends uniquely to $s_j\in F(Z_j)$. Its pullback to $Z$ equals $s$ because both restrict to $x$ on $U$, where the equalizer map is injective. This proves existence of a stage section. We have used $\theta$ only on $A$-morphisms of the fixed systems, not on $d_2$: $d_2$ need not respect the chosen first $A$-structure on $V_i$.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, (1) implies (3), existence (b) on U and eventual equality (a) on V, assembled with the fpqc equalizers.

proof.text: Suppose $s_i\in F(Z_i)$ and $t_j\in F(Z_j)$ have the same pullback to $Z$. Choose $k\ge i,j$ and restrict both to $Z_k$. Their restrictions to $U_k$, interpreted by $\theta_{U_k}$, are two $A$-maps $U_k\to P$ with equal pullbacks to $U$. The eventual-equality lemma for the $U_i$ system gives $l\ge k$ where the two maps, and hence the sections on $U_l$, agree. Injectivity of $F(Z_l)\to F(U_l)$ from Step 3 implies $s_i|_{Z_l}=t_j|_{Z_l}$. This is precisely the asserted sufficiently late common-stage equality.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, (1) implies (3), uniqueness (a) on U, followed by separatedness in the fpqc equalizer condition.

proof.text: The restrictions $F(Z_i)\to F(Z)$ form a cocone and hence induce the canonical map from the colimit. For $s\in F(Z)$ choose a representative $s_i$ from Step 5 and assign its coprojection to the colimit. Step 6 makes this independent of the choice, since two choices have equal images at a common later stage and the colimit cocone identifies them. The composite back to $F(Z)$ is the identity by Step 5. Conversely this assignment composed with restriction sends each stage section to its own coprojection; by the colimit universal property the other composite is the identity on the colimit. Thus the canonical map is a bijection. The argument used no finiteness or separation of $P$ beyond its assumed local finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 01ZC, conclusion from existence and eventual equality; the universal property of the set colimit.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01ZC, proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation, (1) implies (3), applied twice and assembled through the fpqc covering equalizer; Topologies Tag 022D (3).
